To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel network management approach that allows residential network users to dynamically provision QoS services based on SDN and NFVI technologies.

(1) the proposed management model allows users to control their access network resources; (2) the proposed management architecture is based on a user centric approach; (3) the proposed management framework enables users to dynamically provision QoS services; (4) the proposed framework is flexible, easy to deploy, and can be easily extended to new scenarios; and (5) the proposed framework enables the creation of new business models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) how to enable residential users to control the network, and (ii) how to provide traffic differentiation in a residential environment.

the definition of an SDN and NF-based residential network model in which users are able to define and manage their own QoS service requirements and to dynamically allocate the network resources needed to fulfill those requirements.
the development of a novel network management architecture for the dynamic provisioning of traffic differentiation in residential networks based on SDN and NFVs.

we propose an innovative approach to manage the network resources and the traffic differentiation in a residential network based on the use of SDN and cloud technologies.
we have defined a novel network management framework for the dynamic provisioning of differentiated services in a residential network based on a user centric approach.
we propose a novel management model for residential networks that allows users to control access network resources, and to dynamically provision traffic differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model is based on a user-oriented approach that enables residential users to control their own residential network and its resources.
SDN and NFVs technologies can provide the necessary flexibility and programmability to residential networks to allow users to control the network and to define their own QoS requirements.
